rv.q: Ms. Kidman, who turns Franklin’s guardedness into as much a revelation as a concealment of character, is pretty close to perfection.

Dressed almost permanently in a lab coat and often glued to her microscope, [Nicole Kidman] succeeds at capturing the icy intelligence of a woman whose stubborn refusal to hypothesise in place of hard fact (the play alleges) meant that she wound up losing the race....
Grandage's production is a worthy effort, but a little passionless, inherently limited in dramatic force by its subject matter.

cn.t: Kidman delivers a powerful, nuanced performance as Rosalind Franklin that commands attention, though some find Ziegler's play itself underwhelming. Grandage's production earns praise for tackling important subject matter with intelligence.
